subject.title: [Bug]: Isolated cron agentTurn fails with 'setup timed out before runner start' — all fallback models exhausted on 2026.5.12

question: Should OpenClaw accept the bounded derived setup-watchdog behavior in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96219 as the canonical fix for this generic isolated-cron pre-runner timeout, require an operator-configurable watchdog instead, or wait for more live failing traces?
rationale: The source path and field reports show the 60s ceiling is real, but the fix changes how long stuck isolated setup can occupy cron capacity; that tradeoff is a maintainer product/availability decision rather than a mechanical bugfix choice.

options.title: Accept bounded derived watchdog
options.body: Merge the open PR after required checks and treat the longer setup window as the intended default for long isolated cron jobs.

options.title: Require a config knob
options.body: Ask for an operator-tunable setup watchdog if maintainers want slow deployments to opt in rather than changing the default behavior.

options.title: Wait for more live traces
options.body: Keep the issue open without landing the watchdog change until another affected deployment provides a full debug log of the setup phase that stalls.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded derived watchdog
recommendation.body: Merge the open PR after required checks and treat the longer setup window as the intended default for long isolated cron jobs.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest available routing candidate from the likely-owner list for the cron watchdog boundary and the repository's config-surface policy decision.
